clue.text: Unguided writing by unpaid worker?

parts.note: unpaid work is work done for free
a hand is a labourer, as in farmhand or deckhand

explanation.surface: Asks whether a volunteer is responsible for some untutored scrawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing or lettering done without a ruler, stencil or other guiding instrument is done by eye alone.

clue.text: Early trainspotter, booked in 1906

parts.note: the girl in E. Nesbit's 1906 novel The Railway Children who, with her siblings, watches trains pass the cottage; booked means put in a book

explanation.surface: Sounds like a Victorian railway enthusiast holding a ticket from 1906.
explanation.walkthrough: Booked means written into a book, not holding a ticket: Bobbie, eldest of Nesbit's Railway Children, is properly called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesbit's heroine Bobbie spends the novel waving at passing trains, an early kind of train-watching.

clue.text: Prizewinning dramatist eventually made a dogs' dinner

definitions.text: Prizewinning dramatist eventually made a dogs' dinner

parts.words: Prizewinning dramatist eventually made a dogs' dinner
parts.note: an Athenian tragedian who won at the Dionysia and, by ancient legend, was torn apart by hunting dogs in Macedonia

explanation.surface: A celebrated playwright whose later work turned into a complete mess.
explanation.walkthrough: A dog's dinner is British slang for a mess, but here it is literal: legend says the Greek tragedian was killed by King Archelaus's dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek tragic poet won first prize at Athens's dramatic festival and, in the legend, ended up as food for hounds.

clue.text: Mail an unusual version of a leading Orwell character

indicators.note: an unusual version of these letters is a rearranged form of them

explanation.surface: Suggests post forming a strange edition of a main figure from Orwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual version of' rearranges MAIL AN.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's farmyard fable the beasts themselves, pigs and horses, are the principal characters.

clue.text: Set piece by Priestley likely to produce a score?

definitions.text: Set piece by Priestley likely to produce a score?

parts.words: Set piece by Priestley likely to produce a score?
parts.note: a 1932 play by J. B. Priestley, and in football a set piece near the goal that may well lead to a goal being scored

explanation.surface: A Priestley play pictured as a rehearsed football move.
explanation.walkthrough: Set piece is football jargon for a rehearsed restart such as a free kick; a score is a goal. The play title also describes such a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Priestley's drama shares its title with a football commentator's phrase for a threatening kick from the flag.

clue.text: Sillitoe's was solitary

parts.note: Alan Sillitoe's story The Loneliness of the Long Distance ... names a lonely athlete

explanation.surface: Remarks that Sillitoe's figure was a lonely one.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Sillitoe's 1959 story title has 'loneliness' attached to a long-distance athlete; solitary echoes that loneliness.
explanation.definitionFit: The borstal boy in Sillitoe's title is a long-distance athlete, defined by his isolation.

clue.text: He staged a version of Lawrence, but not Shaw

definitions.text: He staged a version of Lawrence, but not Shaw

parts.words: He staged a version of Lawrence, but not Shaw
parts.note: a playwright whose play Ross portrayed T. E. Lawrence under the alias Ross, not his later alias Shaw

explanation.surface: A theatre producer who put on Lawrence but declined Bernard Shaw.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw looks like George Bernard Shaw, but T. E. Lawrence enlisted as both Ross and Shaw; Terence's 1960 play used the name Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence the dramatist wrote Ross, a stage portrait of Lawrence of Arabia under his RAF alias.

clue.text: Nobel laureate novelist suggests new, first-class letter writer

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as AI
Saint Paul wrote the epistles, letters in the New Testament

explanation.surface: A Nobel-winning novelist hints at a fresh, top-quality correspondent.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of A1 is read as the letter I. Letter writer means the apostle whose epistles fill the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: V. S. the Trinidad-born writer won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2001.

clue.text: High level connections produce percentage payments

definitions.meaning: links to kings and queens, read as two words: regal bonds
sums paid to an author or inventor as a share of each sale

explanation.surface: Friends in high places bring in a share of the takings.
explanation.definitionFit: Authors receive a fixed share of sales income, and split in two the word reads as regal links.

clue.text: French farce starts up brightly, unerringly reflecting old intrigues

indicators.note: starts of the following words means their opening letters are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A French comedy opens cheerfully, faithfully mirroring old plots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the first letters of the six words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Jarry's 1896 play is an anarchic, absurd comedy that caused a riot in Paris.

clue.text: Often seen at play in midwinter

definitions.text: Often seen at play in midwinter

parts.words: Often seen at play in midwinter
parts.note: a Christmas school play telling the story of Jesus's birth, staged in December

explanation.surface: Something commonly spotted playing during the depths of winter.
explanation.walkthrough: At play suggests children playing; it means in the school Christmas play, where this word is the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The birth of Christ is the subject of school pageants performed every Christmas.

clue.text: "… Albatros D's and Fokker -—s, I was with von Richtofen" (Jon Cleary, High Road to China)

definitions.text: "… Albatros D's and Fokker -—s, I was with von Richtofen" (Jon Cleary, High Road to China)

parts.words: "… Albatros D's and Fokker -—s, I was with von Richtofen" (Jon Cleary, High Road to China)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: Fokker built a famous three-winged fighter flown by the Red Baron

explanation.surface: A First World War pilot recalls flying German fighters with the Red Baron.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fokker Dr.I was a three-winged aircraft flown by Manfred von Richthofen's squadron.

clue.text: One of the Hispaniola hands

parts.note: in Treasure Island the coxswain of the ship Hispaniola is a pirate whose surname is Hands

explanation.surface: A crew member aboard the ship in Treasure Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Hands looks like crew members in general, but it is the surname of the mutinous coxswain in Stevenson's Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's pirate coxswain is called ... Hands, so this is one of the Hands on that ship.

clue.text: "In — he spilt but seldom blood" (Scott, The Lay of the Last Minstrel)

definitions.text: "In — he spilt but seldom blood" (Scott, The Lay of the Last Minstrel)

parts.words: "In — he spilt but seldom blood" (Scott, The Lay of the Last Minstrel)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap, describing a Border reiver's forays into enemy land

explanation.surface: Scott's line about a Border fighter who rarely drew blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Border reivers made sudden forays to steal cattle, so the gap is filled by such attacks.

clue.text: What Borges's magic may be?

parts.note: the Latin American literary mode called magic realism, applied to writers like Jorge Luis Borges

explanation.surface: Asks what kind of magic the Argentine writer practised.
explanation.walkthrough: Borges is often grouped with magic realism, so his magic might be called realist in style.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic realism describes fiction that treats the fantastic in a matter-of-fact, lifelike way.

clue.text: Find upset (sick) composer

parts.note: to find something is to locate it

indicators.note: upset in a down clue sense means turned over, so the word for sick is read backwards

parts.note: sick means ill

explanation.surface: Asks us to find a composer who is upset and unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ILL into LLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pietro Antonio was an Italian Baroque violinist who wrote concertos and caprices.

clue.text: "He is a sort of —— at the table, serving to stop gaps" (Oliver Wendell Holmes, The Poet at the Breakfast Table)

definitions.text: "He is a sort of —— at the table, serving to stop gaps" (Oliver Wendell Holmes, The Poet at the Breakfast Table)

parts.words: "He is a sort of —— at the table, serving to stop gaps" (Oliver Wendell Holmes, The Poet at the Breakfast Table)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: a filler word inserted only to fill out a line or sentence

explanation.surface: Holmes describes a diner whose role is to fill awkward silences.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a filler word fills a gap in a sentence without adding meaning, as this guest fills pauses.

clue.text: Burns unit

parts.note: a poem addressed by Robert Burns to a small creature, also the name of a computer pointing device

explanation.surface: Looks like a hospital ward for treating burns.
explanation.walkthrough: A burns unit is a hospital ward; here Burns is the Scottish poet and the unit is the creature, or computer device, he addressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Burns's 1785 poem is addressed to a field creature whose nest he turned up with his plough.

clue.text: A roof over the heads of the warden's wards

definitions.text: A roof over the heads of the warden's wards

parts.words: A roof over the heads of the warden's wards
parts.note: in Trollope's The Warden, Mr Harding is warden of Hiram's Hospital, a charitable home for old men

explanation.surface: Describes shelter for the people in a warden's charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Warden and wards suggest a prison, but Trollope's The Warden is set in Hiram's Hospital, a charity home for twelve old bedesmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A charitable home for the aged poor gives them lodging, as Hiram's Hospital does in Trollope.

clue.text: He put women in power in the theatre

definitions.text: He put women in power in the theatre

parts.words: He put women in power in the theatre
parts.note: a playwright and theatre director whose work put women in charge on stage

explanation.surface: A man who gave women positions of authority in theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: John the Scottish playwright founded the 7:84 company and staged political drama.

clue.text: Works like The Odyssey and The Iliad might provide spice

definitions.text: Works like The Odyssey and The Iliad

indicators.note: these letters might provide the answer when reorganised into another order

explanation.surface: Homer's poems are said to add some spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might provide' rearranges SPICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's long narrative poems about heroes are the model of heroic verse.

clue.text: It was instrumental in the development of Greek music

definitions.text: It was instrumental in the development of Greek music

parts.words: It was instrumental in the development of Greek music
parts.note: instrumental read literally: an ancient Greek stringed instrument like a lyre

explanation.surface: Something that played a key role in shaping the music of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: Instrumental usually means influential; here it means literally an instrument, the lyre-like kind played in ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek lyre with a wooden sound box was played by professional musicians.

clue.text: Borders on the ridiculous, this Shakespearean constable

definitions.meaning: borders on means comes close to, as edges or margins do
the bumbling headborough who assists Dogberry in Much Ado About Nothing

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean policeman whose conduct comes close to absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Edges of roads are grassy strips, and comes close to is the verb sense; Dogberry's partner in Much Ado has the same name.

clue.text: Colonel in some footling ramblings from London

indicators.note: in some of the following words means the letters are found inside them

explanation.surface: An army officer appears in some silly wanderings from London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in some' points to the run inside footling ramblings.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel of this surname appears in fiction as a London military figure.

clue.text: David's French dish, not made sans casser des oeufs

definitions.text: David's French dish, not made sans casser des oeufs

parts.words: David's French dish, not made sans casser des oeufs
parts.note: Elizabeth David's book An ... and a Glass of Wine, and the proverb that you cannot make this dish without breaking eggs

explanation.surface: A French dish by David that cannot be made without breaking eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: David is the British cookery writer Elizabeth David. The French phrase means 'without breaking eggs', from the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says the beaten-egg dish cannot be made without breaking eggs, and Elizabeth David titled a book after it.

clue.text: Fall of Keats

parts.note: fall is the American word for the season, and Keats wrote an ode addressed to that season

explanation.surface: Seems to be about the decline of the poet Keats.
explanation.walkthrough: Fall looks like a downfall, but it is the season, and Keats's 1819 ode is addressed to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's ode beginning 'Season of mists and mellow fruitfulness' salutes the harvest season.

clue.text: It gave Segovia and Julian Bream the frets

definitions.text: It gave Segovia and Julian Bream the frets

parts.words: It gave Segovia and Julian Bream the frets
parts.note: frets read literally: the ridges on the fingerboard of the instrument both men played

explanation.surface: Something that worried two great classical musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The frets suggests anxiety; it means the ridges on a fingerboard. Andrés Segovia and Julian Bream were classical players of this instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The six-stringed fretted instrument was played by both virtuosos.

clue.text: Stick together to be consistent in writing

definitions.meaning: to stick together is to hold firmly as one mass
to be logically consistent, as a well-argued text is

explanation.surface: Advice for a team to stay united and make sense on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Particles that cling form a mass, and an argument whose parts fit together is logical.

clue.text: Princely refugee from Happy Valley

parts.note: Samuel Johnson's prince of Abyssinia who escapes the secluded Happy Valley to seek happiness

explanation.surface: A prince fleeing a contented valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Happy Valley is the paradise in Samuel Johnson's 1759 tale where Abyssinian princes are confined until they inherit.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson's Abyssinian prince flees the Happy Valley to search for contentment in the world.
